notes.title: Deck Verified!
notes.notes:
We have just been informed that Charlie Murder passed all the certification tests, and is now officially Verified for Steam Deck!

The game runs exactly as you would expect it to - it's the same native Linux version we've been shipping on Steam since day one, and includes the latest and greatest compatibility work from [url=https://fna-xna.github.io/]FNA[/url]. Work has started to migrate to Vulkan by default to fully maximize energy efficiency, but for now we've found that the game still runs great with the existing renderer.

In case you missed it, [url=https://twitter.com/flibitijibibo/status/1450941262018846725]here's what it looked like when we ran the game locally on the devkit some time ago (along with a bunch of other titles)[/url].

Valve has not fully opened up the certification process just yet, so Dishwasher and Salt will have to wait a bit longer. It's possible that The Algorithm(TM) will pick them up, but we won't know for sure until they e-mail us about it.

Thanks to everyone for their continued support, and we hope you enjoy the game in its new, portable form!

Just one note today:

- Update to latest FNA, includes various improvements and a fix for specific audio filters

- Update to FNA 21.10 (technically releasing Friday, but eh)
- Mostly to work around a Steam Deck OpenGL driver bug, but dramatically improves Vulkan/D3D11 support along the way

notes.title: Have You Played Charlie Murder?
notes.notes:
Have You Played? is an endless stream of game retrospectives. One a day, every day, perhaps for all time.

Despite the occasional highlight that captures the imagination of the masses, beat ‘em ups are sometimes seen as also rans these days. Likewise, punk rock anthems rarely make their way onto the top 40. Ska Studios didn’t let any indifference to either deter them from making three power chord trick video game equivalent Charlie Murder.

notes.title: Charlie Murder, The Dishwasher: Vampire Smile hit PC
notes.notes: Salt and Sanctuary creators Ska Studios have finally brought two of their earlier games to PC, the stabby platformer The Dishwasher: Vampire Smile [official site] and beat ’em up Charlie Murder [official site]. In the traditional Ska way, they’ve got sketchy art, co-op, buckets of moodiness, and shedloads of blood. Vampire Smile hit Xbox 360 via Xbox Live Arcade in 2011 then Charlie Murder followed in 2013, and the two have been slowly heading to PC pretty much ever since. Now they’re here, costing 7 a pop. … [visit site to read more]
